messages:
sam: Quick sync — we need to lock down a TTL strategy for traces across envs. My initial proposal: prod hot tier 90d, prod cold archive 365d, stage 30d hot then delete after 90d, dev 7d then delete. Also want to route expensive cold read queries through a separate quota/cost bucket. Thoughts? @elaine @jordan
elaine: Broadly ok but need to define query SLOs for cold reads first. If dashboards start hitting cold we should surface cost to dashboard owners.
jordan: I'd prefer per-service priority tags instead of just env. Some infra services are "prod-low" but still need 90d. Maybe combine environment + priority label -> TTL matrix.
priya: Agree on priority labels. We can add a boolean on spans: service.priority = [high|medium|low]. Then retention policy = lookup(env, service.priority). Also we should consider keeping root spans + error traces longer than regular traces.
mike: Cost note: cold storage costs are small, egress and rehydration cost more. If we force frequent cold reads we'll blow the budget. Suggest: cold reads require approval or a special billing tag so PMs see it.
sam: Good points. Operationally we also need exporter and collector changes. Suggest the collector attach `rt.ttl_policy` attr during ingest based on lookup table. Example mapping in the collector config:```yamlreceivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc: {}
processors:
  attributes:
    actions:
      - key: rt.ttl_policy
        action: insert
        value: |
          env=${env};priority=${service.priority}
exporters:
  redis-ttl:
    endpoint: redis://traces-ttl:6379```This is rough but shows intent.
priya: Slight tweak — don't rely only on incoming span attrs. We should enrich using service metadata service-registry join to avoid noisy instrumentation changes. Collector can call the service catalog to set priority if missing.
elaine: For dashboards: add a Grafana panel that shows expected monthly cold-read cost per dashboard and a per-query cost alert. Make it visible to dashboard owners via annotations.
tracebot: retention-controller scheduled job created: retention-evaluator v1. Will run daily to mark trace objects for cold transition. Logs: next-run 2026-06-14T12:00:00Z.
mike: About migration — for existing traces we need a backfill job to classify by priority and move to cold tier if older than threshold. Estimate ~48h run with throttling. Any objections?
jordan: No objections. Need to ensure query engine returns a clear header when results are from cold/archived — so apps can degrade gracefully.
sam: Rollout plan draft: 1) Implement collector enrichment and attribute insertion behind feature flag; 2) Create retention-evaluator job v1 and dry-run for 7 days (mark-only); 3) Backfill job with throttling; 4) Enable auto-transition and enforce cold-read quotas; 5) Update dashboards/alerts and publish playbook. Canary: one non-customer-facing namespace first (analytics), then small-prod slice.
priya: Also add sampling changes: increase tail-sampling retention for high-priority services and aggressive sampling for low-priority dev services. We'll include sampling params in the playbook.
elaine: UX: Add a rollout toggle in Console > Telemetry > Retention so support can pause/unpause transitions per-org. Also export an audit log for any manual promotes/deletes.
sam: OK I'll draft the playbook. Action items: @priya to spec collector enrichment, @jordan to draft priority matrix, @elaine to sketch cost dashboard, @mike to scope backfill. Deploybot: can you create a ticket template for rollout?
deploybot: created ticket TD-8142 with checklist and rollback steps.
tracebot: FYI: archive format will be compressed protobuf blobs + metadata index. Query path will return a 304-like metadata-only entry for cold traces until rehydrate is requested.
sam: Thanks all. If nobody objects by EOD I'll open a PR with the collector changes and playbook. :thumbsup:
